## The one local edit to a vendored check — and why it was unavoidable

`scripts/check-assets.mjs` carries **one** change from v3.7.1, marked in place. Everything else in
`scripts/` is byte-identical to the release; `scripts/.vendored.sha256` proves it and the gate
verifies it.

**The defect.** `ratchet.mjs --init` writes `.gate-baseline.json` at the scanned root. Its keys embed
asset paths — `"check-assets|images/hero-fondo.png"`. `check-assets` scans every `.json` file for
references, matches those substrings, and reports each one as *referenced but not committed*. So the
ratchet's first run writes a file that makes its second run fail: measured here, 53 findings became
73 with 20 spurious increases, and the gate would have been red forever on its own artifact. That is
the exact failure the ratchet exists to prevent.

**The change.** One filter clause excluding `.gate-baseline.json` from the reference scan. It does
not weaken a rule or silence a finding: `walk()` already skips `scripts/` and `.github/` because
they are gate machinery, and this file is gate machinery that happens to live at the root.

**This belongs upstream, not here.** It affects every site that adopts with an asset finding, which
is all of them. Reported as handbook feedback (§12). **Revert this edit and re-take the file from
the release that fixes it** — that is the trigger, and the hash pin is what will make the revert
visible.

## Deliberately NOT taken, with the reason

A rule file that arrives is easy to see. One that never arrived is invisible unless it is written
down, which is what this section is for.

- **`facts.js` + `scripts/build-derived.mjs`.** The single-source derivation of markup, structured
  data and `llms.txt`. This site holds those facts in three independent places today, and adopting
  the mechanism means rewriting `index.html` — which is code, and step 1 of the adoption procedure
  touches none. Recorded as **DEBT-04**.
- **`site.js`.** Builds external destinations from `config.js` so the markup carries a key and never
  a URL. Same reason; it is the other half of **DEBT-01**.
- **`analytics.js` (the template's).** This repository already has one of its own, with a different
  contract — it has no consent default and no intent/outcome split. Overwriting it is a behaviour
  change on a live site. Recorded as **DEBT-06** and **FIX-04**.
- **`_headers`, `_redirects`.** Netlify-style files that do nothing on Apache and nothing on GitHub
  Pages either. The migration decided on 2026-08-11 moves to a host that serves **no custom headers
  and issues no real redirects at all** — so these are not deferred, they are foreclosed. That is the
  cost side of **OPEN-03**, recorded there rather than discovered later.
- **`lighthouserc.json`.** The performance and accessibility floors. Part of **DEBT-14**, whose
  trigger is the image debt landing — a floor that fails from day one is a floor somebody removes.
- ~~**`privacy.html`, `404.html`, `.nojekyll`.**~~ **All three now exist**, written for this site
  rather than copied: `privacy.html` with FIX-02, and `404.html` + `.nojekyll` with the move to
  GitHub Pages. `.nojekyll` is §26's "disable host processing nobody asked for" — Jekyll silently
  drops paths beginning with `_` or `.`, and files nobody notices are missing is exactly the
  failure mode §26 names.
- **`scripts/test-gate.mjs`.** Taken, found unrunnable here, and removed with the reason recorded as
  **INAPPLICABLE-01**. It builds fixtures by copying the repository around it and editing the
  template's placeholder values; in an adopting repository those values are real and the setup
  throws before any check runs. It tests the checks, the checks are maintained upstream, and that is
  where it runs. What it covered here — a check edited locally to silence a finding — is covered by
  the hash pin instead.
- **`brief.md`.** Taken and filled — see the file. It is where the six irreversibles are recorded,
  and four of the six are unanswered here.
- **OpenSpec workspace (§19).** Not adopted in this pass. The spec-driven lifecycle applies to this
  class, and its absence is recorded as **OPEN-04** rather than assumed away.

## Re-syncing

`AGENTS.md` and `scripts/*.mjs` are generated upstream. Re-take them from a released tag, never edit
them here, and update the frontmatter above in the same commit. If a rule in `AGENTS.md` is wrong,
the handbook is where it changes.
